h: Snow, water gardens and a few wonky holes
p: Hemel is one of the post-war new towns, rebuilt and expanded from the late 1940s onwards, and that gives it a bit of an unusual mix: a modern centre with an old town tucked beside it. It also means there's plenty of leisure packed into one place, and crazy golf sits nicely alongside the other indoor options in town. The Snow Centre at Jarman Park is the obvious partner if you've got an active family who want to ski or toboggan on real snow on the same weekend.

In the town centre, look out for the Water Gardens, a long, landscaped stretch alongside the River Gade designed by the landscape architect Geoffrey Jellicoe. They've been restored in recent years and make a calm spot for a sit-down and a sandwich between activities.

As for the golf itself, allow about an hour for a round with a normal-sized group, and give yourself a bit of slack if you're bringing a crowd. A quick tip for parents: let the youngest go first on each hole. It keeps them engaged, stops the queue of fidgety kids building up, and gives the grown-ups a chance to plan their sneaky trick shots.

If you're making a weekend of it, Hemel is well placed for bigger days out. The Ashridge Estate, with its woodlands and the Bridgewater Monument, is a short drive away, Berkhamsted has the ruins of its Norman castle by the railway station, and the Warner Bros. Studio Tour at Leavesden, home of the Harry Potter sets, is not far either.
